items.title: Show HN: HocusFocus – Pomodoro timer and Lofi Music player for your Mac's notch
items.contentSnippet:
I built an app that shows a Pomodoro timer and Lofi Music channels under your Mac's notch, for quick and easy access. The timer slips away as part of the notch so you just see the countdown, and pops up on hover when you need it.
My motivation for building this was to help me set dedicated focus times during my day. I find Lofi music from the Lofi Girl channel especially useful to get my brain focused.

items.title: Show HN: Xtriever – offline RAG retrieval on a phone
items.contentSnippet:
For anyone doing local (or not) RAG: I built Xtriever, the retrieval half of the problem, designed to run on the device with no server.
Usable from Rust, Python, Swift and Kotlin. There are demo apps for iOS and Android and a Python CLI.
It’s not production ready yet so for now build from source only.
Android is measured only on the emulator, and there's no learned ranker yet.
This thing is purely vibecoded.

items.title: Show HN: Giving my inner monologue autocomplete, with my own voice
items.contentSnippet:
I built a website that makes you hear the voices in your head. They will complete your thoughts, in all the ways they might have unfolded, with your own voice. Everything runs locally in your browser.
I wanted the experience to be 1) local 2) realtime and 3) with voice cloning. Under the hood it’s VAD -> STT -> LLM -> TTS, respectively:
- Silero
- Parakeet CTC 0.6B
- LFM2.5-350
⁃ Pocket TTS
Ofc, they're not technically your thoughts. I finetuned the LLM on Simone Weil’s and Albert Camus’s person
